headline: IBM updates Granite Switch without retraining
dek: The new version ships as adapters and leaves the base model intact, per IBM.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: An incremental update
body: IBM released Granite Switch 4.1.1 a week after 4.1, per a statement on Hugging Face.
The company says it is fully compatible with the prior version and needs no migration (Hugging Face).

points.t: The base model stays frozen and is not recomputed.
Each adapter adds one specific capability.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: What is new
body: IBM trained only a speech recognition model and a decision adapter (Hugging Face).
The company compares the swap to a software update: users pick adapters and redeploy.

items.t: IBM is building an Adapter SDK, with no date.
Pricing and license were not disclosed.

caption.hook: IBM updated Granite Switch to version 4.1.1 without retraining the base model.
body: Per IBM, on Hugging Face, the architecture is modular: new capabilities arrive as adapters attached to a frozen base model. For 4.1.1, the company trained only a speech recognition model and a decision adapter.

The update is compatible with 4.1 and needs no migration. IBM is preparing tutorials and an Adapter SDK so third parties can build their own adapters, with no date set. The statement discloses no pricing or license and does not say whether the kit will work with other companies' models.
caption.cta: Would modular AI updates change how you use models?
